text: Let's start the interview now. Tell me a little bit about yourself.
Please describe the place where you live. What does it look like, and which room do you like the most? Tell me in as much detail as possible.
You indicated that you go to the park. What do you usually do when you go there? Who do you go with, and when do you usually go?
Tell me about a memorable trip you took in your country. Where did you go, who were you with, and what happened that made it so memorable?
When did you first become interested in music? What kind of music did you listen to back then, and how has your taste changed since?
How are cafes today different from the cafes you went to a few years ago? Compare the atmosphere, menus, and the way people use them.
What kind of movies do you like to watch? Tell me about your favorite genre and why you enjoy it.
Tell me about your jogging or walking routine. Where do you go, how often, and what do you do before and after exercising?
Tell me about how people recycle in your country. What do people usually recycle, and how do they do it?
Technology has changed the way people live. What is one piece of technology that people commonly use these days, and what concerns do people have about it?
I'd like to give you a situation and ask you to act it out. You want to join a new gym. Call the gym and ask three or four questions to get the information you need.

I'm sorry, but there is a problem. You bought two concert tickets for you and your friend, but something came up and you can't go. Call your friend, explain the situation, and suggest two or three alternatives.
Have you ever had a situation where your plans were canceled or something went wrong with a reservation? Tell me what happened and how you dealt with it.
Describe a restaurant you visit often. Where is it, what is it like, and why do you go there?
Tell me about a time you missed a bus or train. What happened, and what did you do next?
How has your neighborhood changed over the past few years? Describe what it was like before and what it is like now.
You registered for a fitness class, but the center changed the schedule. Call the center, explain the problem, ask questions, and suggest an alternative.
What is one pedestrian safety problem near a school in your community, and what could people do to improve the situation?
Describe a mobile app you use frequently. Explain its main features and why it is useful to you.
You bought a jacket, but it is the wrong size. Call the store, explain the problem, and ask about an exchange or refund.
You made an appointment for a haircut, but your schedule has changed. Call the salon and reschedule it.
Describe a book you enjoyed. What happened in the story, and why was it memorable?
Describe a festival or community event you attended. What did you see and do there?
Tell me about a time bad weather changed your outdoor plans. Explain how you adjusted.
Tell me about a time you lost something valuable. How did you look for it, and what happened?
Describe a place where you like to study or concentrate. What is it like, and why do you prefer it?
Describe a volunteer activity you participated in. What did you do, and what did you learn?
Tell me how you became friends with someone important to you. What happened when you first met?
How has the way you communicate with family and friends changed since you were younger?
Do you prefer shopping online or in physical stores? Explain your opinion with examples.
Describe a meal you tried to cook yourself. What went well or wrong, and how did it turn out?
Tell me about a sports event you watched in person. What happened, and why do you remember it?
Do you enjoy taking photographs? Describe what you usually photograph and one picture you remember.
Describe a problem you had while working on a group project. How did your team resolve it?
There is a water leak in your apartment. Call the property manager, explain the situation, and request assistance.
A visitor asks how to get from the subway station to the city museum. Give directions and explain an alternative if a street is closed.
Your city is considering building a new cultural center. Do you support the plan? Explain your opinion and address possible concerns.
Tell me about a time you changed the furniture or layout in your home. What did you change, why did you change it, and how did it turn out?
How does your family share household chores these days? Compare your responsibilities now with the chores you did when you were younger. What has changed, and why?
Describe a beach you enjoy visiting. Where is it, what do you normally do there, and can you tell me about a visit that you especially remember?
Describe the bank you usually use. What is the branch like, how do you use its services, and how has the way you bank changed over time?
You need to replace a bank card that you have lost. Call your bank and ask three or four questions about the identification you need, the replacement process, and when you can get the new card.
Think about the dentist you went to when you were young and the one you visit now. How are they similar or different, and how has your experience of dental visits changed?
Tell me about a memorable visit to a hospital or clinic. Why did you need to go, what problem came up, and how did you handle the situation?
What is your major, and what kind of semester project are you working on? Describe the project, the difficulties you faced, and how you and your team dealt with them.
What is the geography of your country like? Describe its major geographical features and explain which natural landscapes make it special to visitors.
Tell me about an outdoor activity you did in a place with unusual natural features. Where did you go, what did you do there, and what made the experience memorable?
How have clothing styles and fashion trends changed from when you were younger to today? Explain what has stayed the same and what is different.
Compare singers and composers. What do they have in common, how are their roles different, and how do they contribute to a song?
You want to buy two tickets for a concert. Call the concert venue and ask three or four questions about available seats, prices, and how to make the purchase.
Tell me about the most memorable concert you have attended. When and where was it, who went with you, and what happened that made it stand out?
A friend tells you that their family has opened a restaurant. Call your friend and ask three or four questions about the food, location, hours, and services before you visit.
You ordered food for delivery, but the wrong meal arrived. Call the restaurant, explain what happened, and suggest two possible ways to fix the problem.
Tell me about an especially memorable experience with food delivery. What did you order, who were you with, and what happened that made it memorable?
Tell me about a time something went wrong while you were using a bank service. Describe the problem, what you did, and how it was resolved.
You rent an apartment, and a window has been damaged. Call your landlord, explain the damage and why it needs attention, and ask for a practical repair arrangement.
You borrowed an e-book reader from a friend, but you cannot find it now. Call your friend, explain what happened, apologize, and offer ways to make up for the loss.
You accidentally broke a music player that a friend lent you. Call your friend, explain the damage, and suggest two or three reasonable ways to resolve the problem.
You are using a computer at the public library, but it has stopped working. Speak to a librarian, explain the problem and why you need the computer, and ask for help or an alternative.
You are thinking of buying a laptop for school and work. Call an electronics store and ask several questions about the laptop's specifications, price, warranty, and availability.
Compare how students used technology for learning in the past with how they use it today. What has changed about classes, assignments, and communication with teachers?
Think about the first mobile phone you owned and the smartphone you use now. What could each device do, and how has your daily use of a phone changed?
You cannot sign in to an important website you need for your classes. Contact its support staff, explain the error, and ask for help and a way to proceed if it cannot be fixed immediately.
Tell me about a time you had difficulty using a new website. What were you trying to do, what went wrong, and how did you finally solve the problem?
How has the use of electronic devices at school changed since you were younger? Compare your earlier study habits with how you study and submit work today.
Some jobs have changed or disappeared because of new technology. Describe a few examples, explain why this is happening, and share your opinion about the changes.
Tell me about an important industry in your country, such as semiconductors. How has it developed, and what factors have helped it grow?
Think about a newly released electronic product. What makes a product launch successful or unsuccessful? Explain the factors you would consider and give examples.
Tell me about a recent development in artificial intelligence or another technology that interests you. What can it be used for, and what effects might it have on people's lives?
Food contamination can cause serious problems. What should people do at home and what should restaurants do to keep food safe? Explain your ideas.
What do you usually do to stay healthy? Describe your daily habits, why you follow them, and how they affect the way you feel.
Tell me about a particularly memorable vacation you spent at home. How did you spend your time, who was involved, and why do you remember it?
Describe a major holiday in your country and how your family celebrates it. What do you usually do together, and has the way you celebrate changed?
Imagine that your class has an outdoor activity planned, but rain is expected. Talk to your teacher, explain your concerns, and suggest at least two alternative plans.
A gym class you paid for has been canceled. Contact the gym, explain your situation, and ask for a makeup class, a refund, or another reasonable solution.
You want to meet a nutrition counselor to discuss your diet. Call the office, ask three or four questions about the appointment, preparation, and services, and arrange a suitable time.
You need to make a dental appointment. Call the dental clinic and ask about available dates, the appointment process, and what you should prepare.
Your car is having a problem and you need repairs. Call an auto repair shop, describe the symptoms, and ask about inspection, repair time, and scheduling.
You have an upcoming job interview. Call the company and ask several questions about the interview format, location, schedule, and what you should bring.
You have a job interview scheduled, but an unexpected conflict means you cannot attend at that time. Call the company, explain the situation politely, and request a new appointment.
Tell me about a time you were late for an important appointment or meeting. What caused the delay, how did you let the others know, and what happened afterward?
Tell me about a time you had trouble learning to use a new piece of technology. What made it difficult, how did you learn to use it, and what was the result?
Housing costs and finding a place to live can be challenging. What are some housing problems people face in your country, and what could be done to improve the situation?
Choose two parks in your country that you know. Compare their location, facilities, atmosphere, and the activities people can enjoy there.
Choose two members of your family. Describe their personalities and daily habits, and explain their similarities and differences with examples.
Compare visiting a close friend's home with visiting a relative's home. What is similar about the visits, and how are the atmosphere and activities different?
Compare the home you lived in as a child with the one you live in now. How did your family use the rooms and space then, and how is it different today?
Compare traveling a long distance by train and by express bus. What are the advantages and disadvantages of each, and which do you prefer?
How is taking public transportation during rush hour different from taking it in the middle of the day? Describe the differences in crowds, comfort, and travel time.
Compare the ways you listened to music as a child with the way you listen now. What devices and services did you use then, and how are they different today?
Compare finding information in a library with searching for it on the internet. What is useful about each method, and when would you choose one over the other?
Compare a busy beach near a city with a quieter natural beach. What do they have in common, and how are the facilities, scenery, and experience different?
Compare studying in an online class with attending a class in person. How are the learning experience and interaction with the teacher different?
Think about family trips you took as a child and trips you plan yourself today. What has changed about the planning, responsibilities, and experience?
Compare watching a movie alone at home and going to a movie theater with friends. What are the benefits and drawbacks of each experience?
You want to join a chess gathering with a friend. Call your friend and ask three or four questions about where and when to meet, what to bring, and who will be there.
A new public library has opened in your neighborhood. Call the library and ask several questions about getting a membership and the rules for using its facilities.
You want to order groceries online from a supermarket. Call the store and ask three or four questions about delivery areas, fees, times, and ordering procedures.
You are planning to visit a movie theater with someone who uses a wheelchair. Call the theater and ask about accessible entrances, seats, and other assistance.
You are flying overseas soon. Call the airline and ask a few questions about baggage allowances, connecting flights, and what you should do during a transfer.
You want to try a beginner's swimming class. Call a swimming pool and ask about class times, prices, a trial lesson, and what equipment you need.
You need a copy of your medical records from a hospital. Call the records office and ask how to request the documents, what identification is needed, and when they will be ready.
You are interested in a robotics workshop at a science and technology center. Call and ask about the schedule, registration requirements, materials, and fees.
You want to volunteer at a local festival. Call the organizer and ask about available duties, work hours, registration, and any training required.
You are considering renting a small apartment. Call the landlord or agent and ask about the rent, maintenance fees, and who is responsible for repairs.
You arranged to meet a friend at a park, but the park has closed for an event. Call your friend, explain what happened, and suggest two alternative places or plans.
You borrowed your friend's earphones, but one side has stopped working. Call your friend, apologize, explain the situation, and offer a couple of ways to fix it.
You bought concert tickets online and were charged twice. Call customer service, explain the duplicate payment, and request a refund or another workable solution.
A yoga class scheduled outdoors was canceled because of rain. Contact the organizer, explain the inconvenience, and ask about a makeup session or refund.
You planned to visit a friend's family, but the time you agreed on no longer works. Call your friend, explain the change, and suggest an alternative arrangement.
You are staying at a hotel, but the internet connection in your room does not work and you have an online meeting soon. Call the front desk and ask for a practical solution.
The train you planned to take to the airport has been canceled. Call your travel companion, explain the situation, and suggest other ways to get to the airport on time.
You are running late for a hospital appointment. Call the hospital, explain the delay, and ask whether you can arrive late or reschedule.
You notice that a photo caption in a local festival brochure is incorrect. Contact the organizer, explain the mistake, and suggest how they could correct it.
You rented a tent at a campsite, but its zipper is broken. Speak to the staff, explain the problem, and request another tent or an acceptable alternative.
Describe a large supermarket you know in your country. What is the place like, what services does it offer, and how do people usually shop there?
Describe the hospital or clinic you usually visit. What does it look like, and what steps do you follow from checking in to seeing the doctor?
Describe a local festival venue you have visited. What was the atmosphere like, and what kinds of food stalls, performances, and activities could people enjoy?
Describe a walking trail near a river or the sea. What does the landscape look like, and what do people usually do there?
Describe your university library. How are the study areas and book collections arranged, and how do students use the facilities?
What do you think students should keep in mind when using generative AI for school assignments? Explain what responsible use means to you and give examples.
What should visitors do to protect natural places such as beaches and mountains? Explain why it matters and what individuals and local authorities can do.
If your city could improve one part of its public transportation system, what should it focus on? Explain the problem and the changes you would recommend.
What difficulties do young people face when trying to find a place to live? Describe the main cost and information problems and suggest ways to improve them.
People often look up health advice on the internet. What are the advantages and risks of doing that, and when should they seek professional advice instead?
Tell me about a time the electricity suddenly went out while you were preparing dinner or spending the evening at home. What happened, and how did your family manage?
Tell me about a time your internet connection failed when you needed to submit an assignment. What did you do to finish and submit your work?
Tell me about a holiday when your family's visiting plans changed unexpectedly. Why did they change, and what did your family do instead?
Tell me about a time you helped a visitor or tourist while volunteering at a local event. What did the person need, and how did you help?
Tell me about a time a technical problem interrupted a movie at the theater. What happened during the screening, and how did the staff and audience respond?
Tell me about a camping trip when something at the campsite made it difficult to sleep or relax. What was the problem, and how did you handle it?
Tell me about a time you lost important data during a school laboratory session or project. What did you lose, and how did you recover or finish your work?
Tell me about a time you misunderstood where you were supposed to meet a friend. Why did the mix-up happen, and how did you resolve it?
Compare going to a bank branch in person with using mobile banking. What services can you get through each, and what are the pros and cons?
Compare libraries you visited as a child with modern libraries that use digital technology. How have borrowing books and using the facilities changed?
Compare seeing a live performance in a small venue with attending a large concert. How do the atmosphere and audience experience differ?
Compare studying by yourself with studying in a group. What are the advantages and disadvantages of each approach, and which works better for you?
Compare cooking a meal at home with ordering food for delivery. What is convenient or difficult about each, and when do you prefer one over the other?
Compare using a rental car with taking public transportation when traveling. How do they differ in convenience, cost, and the places you can visit?
Compare the video games you played when you were younger with the mobile games people play today. How are the devices and gaming experiences different?
Compare using a paper ticket and a mobile QR-code ticket at a performance. What is similar about the two, and what are the advantages and problems of each?
Choose a busy area of your city. Compare what it looks and feels like during the day and at night. What activities take place at each time?
Compare working or studying at home with using a shared workspace. How do the two environments affect your focus, convenience, and interaction with others?
You have just moved into an apartment building. Call the management office and ask several questions about recycling days, sorting rules, and where to put different kinds of waste.
You want to take a beginner's foreign-language class at a community center. Call the center and ask about registration, the schedule, tuition, and class requirements.
You will arrive at an unfamiliar train station while traveling abroad. Call the station and ask about luggage storage, the last train, and how to get to your destination.
You have an upcoming flight and need information about special meals and changing your booking. Call the airline and ask three or four relevant questions.
You are organizing a museum visit with classmates. Call the museum and ask about group admission, audio guides, reservations, and visiting hours.
You want to use equipment in a university makerspace for a project. Call or speak to the staff and ask about borrowing rules, safety training, and access hours.
An electronic device you bought recently needs repair. Call the service center and ask about the warranty, the repair procedure, and how long it might take.
You are thinking about joining a university photography club. Call a club member and ask about recruitment, meeting times, equipment, and activities.
You want to attend a theater performance with a relative who needs hearing assistance. Call the venue and ask about listening devices, seating, and arrangements for visitors.
You want to rent a bicycle during a trip. Call the rental shop and ask about fees, rental hours, safety equipment, and what happens if there is an accident.

You reserved a quiet meeting room for an online interview, but another group is using it when you arrive. Speak to the coworking-space staff, explain the problem, and ask for another quiet room or a workable alternative.
You are about to give a class presentation, but the projector will not display your slides. Talk to your professor or the classroom staff, explain the problem, and suggest a way to continue.
You booked a train ticket for the wrong date. Call the rail company, explain your mistake, and ask how to change the ticket or obtain another solution.
You received an electronic product you ordered, but an accessory that should have been included is missing. Contact the seller, explain what is missing, and request a replacement or another solution.
Your team is due to give a presentation today, but one member is unexpectedly absent. Talk to your professor, explain the situation, and suggest how the team can proceed.
A seminar you are helping with has suddenly changed locations, and overseas visitors need updated directions. Contact a visitor, explain the change, and suggest how to reach the new venue.
You have booked museum tickets on your phone, but the QR code does not work at the entrance. Speak to the staff, explain the problem, and ask for a way to enter.
You planned to hike with friends, but part of the trail has been closed for safety reasons. Call your friends, explain the closure, and suggest another safe route or activity.
You have an exam tomorrow, but loud noise from a neighboring apartment is keeping you awake. Call your building's management office, explain the situation politely, and ask for help.
You are at the gym and cannot open your locker, even though you are using the correct code. Ask the staff for help and explain why you need access to your belongings soon.
Describe a makerspace or workshop at your university. What areas and equipment does it have, and how do students use the space from check-in to finishing a project?
Describe a large railway station you know. What are the waiting areas, ticket facilities, and transfer signs like, and how do travelers find their way around?
Describe a traditional market during a major holiday season in your country. What does it look and sound like, and what do you usually see or buy there?
Describe a night market near a river or another public area. What are the food stalls, performances, and places to sit like, and why do people go there?
Describe a local public health center. What facilities and health programs does it offer, and how do visitors usually use its services?
Popular tourist destinations can benefit from visitors but also create problems for local residents. How should communities balance tourism and residents' daily lives?
What could cities do to make public facilities more accessible to people with disabilities? Explain the improvements you think are most important and why.
Online platforms collect a lot of information about students. What privacy problems can this cause, and what should schools and students do to protect that information?
Some cities are considering more late-night public transportation. Do you think this is a good idea? What benefits and challenges should city planners consider?
Local events often depend on volunteers. What could organizers do to encourage more residents to volunteer, and why would those methods work?
Tell me about a memorable time you volunteered at a community event. What were you supposed to do, what unexpected situation came up, and how did you handle it?
Have you ever returned to a neighborhood you knew when you were younger? Describe what happened during your visit, what had changed, and how you felt.
Describe a time something went wrong while you were preparing a meal for family or friends. What was the problem, what did you do, and how did the event end?
Tell me about a time an important personal item broke right before something you needed to do. What happened, and how did you manage the situation?
Describe a time you misunderstood the schedule of an online meeting or activity. Why did the mistake happen, and what did you do?
Tell me about a problem you experienced at a hotel or guesthouse while traveling. What was wrong, how did you explain it, and what happened afterward?
Tell me about a visit to a hospital or clinic that did not go as planned. Explain what happened and how you handled the unexpected change.
Have you ever helped a visitor or stranger in a place you know well? Describe the situation, what the person needed, and how you helped.
Tell me about a time something you bought on a trip was damaged or lost. What was it, what did you do, and how did the situation turn out?
Compare how people used to find directions with paper maps and how they use navigation apps today. What do the two methods have in common, and what are the differences?
Compare the shopping streets you remember from the past with large shopping malls today. How are their stores, atmosphere, and shopping habits similar or different?
Think about a holiday your family celebrates and a holiday tradition you have learned about from someone abroad. What is similar about them, and how are they different?
Compare walking along a mountain trail with walking beside the sea. What do you enjoy about each place, and how do the experiences differ?
Some people spend vacation time at home, while others travel to another city. Compare these two ways of spending a vacation, including their advantages and disadvantages.
Compare attending a festival in person with watching the same event online. What can you experience in each situation, and what are the main differences?
Compare learning about a famous person through a printed magazine interview and through a video interview. How are they alike, and how do they differ?
Compare living in an apartment building and living in a detached house. What are some similarities and differences in daily life?
Compare what you normally do in your free time on a weekday evening with what you do on weekends. How do the activities and atmosphere differ?
How do outdoor activities in your area change between summer and winter? Compare the weather, the places people visit, and the activities they do.
You have heard about a local hiking club and want to join. Call the organizer and ask three or four questions about the routes, meeting times, and what you need to bring.
You plan to visit a museum while carrying a suitcase. Call the museum and ask about luggage storage, opening hours, and other services you might need.
You are interested in an overseas internship program. Call the program coordinator and ask about eligibility, application documents, and the program schedule.
You want to sell or exchange some textbooks at a bookstore. Call and ask about accepted books, payment, and store credit.
Your apartment building has announced a temporary water shutoff. Call the management office and ask about the schedule and how residents should prepare.
You want to travel by intercity bus and take your bicycle with you. Call the bus terminal and ask about baggage rules, fees, and available departures.
You would like to take a beginner photography workshop. Call the instructor and ask what equipment is required, how the class works, and how to register.
You want to visit a local food festival with friends who have different food preferences. Call the organizer and ask about menu information and services.

Describe a science or engineering exhibition at a university. What do visitors see, how do they explore the exhibits, and what interests you most?
Describe what your home kitchen is like when your family prepares a holiday meal. What does the space look and sound like, and what does everyone do?
Describe a post office you use and explain what you normally do when you send a package. What is the place like, and what steps do you follow?
Describe an outdoor sports court or field that people use near your home. What facilities are there, what do people do, and what is the atmosphere like?
What changes would make walking to school or work safer in your city? Explain the problems you see and suggest practical improvements.

Hi, my name is Minji. I'm a third-year computer science student in Busan. I live with my family near campus, so I usually walk to school. In my free time I listen to music because it helps me relax.

Well, I live in an apartment in Busan with my family. Our apartment is on the tenth floor, so the view is pretty good. When you open the door, you can see the living room first. There is a big sofa and a TV, and my family usually watch TV there after dinner. We have three bedrooms and two bathrooms. My favorite room is my bedroom because it is my own space. For example, I study, play games and sometimes watch YouTube there. Actually, it is a little small, but I really like it.

Well, I usually go to the park near my house on weekends. I go there with my dog, because he really love walking outside. First, we walk around the lake for about an hour. There are a lot of people who jogging or riding bikes, so it is very lively. After walking, I sit on a bench and listen to music. Sometimes my friend join me and we eat some snacks together. I usually go in the evening because the weather is cooler and the sunset is beautiful. Actually, it is the best way to relieve my stress.

I want to talk about my trip to Jeju Island last summer. I went there with my family for three days. On the first day, we go to Hyeopjae Beach. The water was really clear and blue, so we swim for a long time. On the second day, we climbed Hallasan. It is very hard because it takes about eight hours, but when we arrive at the top, the view is amazing. Also, we ate black pork for dinner and it was so delicious. Actually, it was our first family trip in five years, so it was very special for me.

Well, cafes today are really different from a few years ago. In the past, most cafes was small and the interior was simple. The menu was mostly coffee, like americano or latte. But these days, cafes are bigger and more stylish, so people take a lot of pictures for Instagram. Also, there are so many desserts, for example, croffles and fancy cakes. Another big change is how people use cafes. Before, people just meet friends and talk, but now many students study there for hours. Actually, I also study at a cafe almost every day.

Hi, how are you? I'm calling because I just moved to this neighborhood and I'm looking for a gym. I saw your gym on the internet, so I have some questions. First, how much is the membership? Actually, I'm a student, so is there any student discount? Second, what time do you open in the morning? Because I have class at nine, I want to work out early. Also, do you have group classes like yoga or pilates? And lastly, can I use a locker and towel for free? Okay, thank you so much. I will visit tomorrow.

Hey, it's me. I'm so sorry, but I have some bad news. I can't go to the concert on Saturday, because my cousin's wedding is that day. I totally forgot about it, and my parents said I have to go. I know you was really excited. So, I have some ideas. First, you can take both tickets and go with Minji, because she likes that singer too. Or I can sell the tickets online and give you the money. Also, the singer has another concert next month, so maybe we can go together then. Call me back, okay?

I think the most common technology these days is the smartphone. Almost everyone have one, and we use it for everything, like searching, shopping and banking. But people have some worries about it. The biggest concern is addiction. For example, when I take the subway, almost everyone is looking at their phone, and nobody talk to each other. Also, many kids spend too much time on YouTube, so parents are worried. Another problem is privacy, because apps collect a lot of our personal information. Actually, I also use my phone too much, so I am trying to reduce my screen time.
